look_here_first: CHECK THE TRUE NECTAR GLAND, NOT THE VARIABLE LEAVES. Euphorbia heterophylla (painted spurge) has usually GREEN or pale-green upper bracts, often highly variable leaf outlines, a smooth developing THREE-LOBED capsule, and ONE yellow-green cyathial nectar gland with a RAISED CIRCULAR/ANNULAR RIM. The exact saved SAplants var. heterophylla macro now SHOWS and annotates that ROUND rimmed gland opening. E. cyathophora normally has red/pink/white patches at bract bases, but some plants have all-green bracts; its gland is distinctly OBLONG and lacks the raised circular rim. The salmon-pink-bracted older Psumuseum photograph labeled E. heterophylla is on TAXON ID HOLD, so do not teach from or publish that image until identity is resolved. Nativity/range status unchanged.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Approved comparison-only taxon; POWO/FNA treat Texas occurrence as introduced/naturalized. Exclude from native metrics.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia: milky latex; the apparent flower is a cyathium with highly reduced male flowers and one central female flower.
morphology_keys.leaves: Highly polymorphic within populations and even on one plant; blades may be lanceolate, elliptic, obovate, pandurate, or lobed. Leaf shape alone is unreliable.
morphology_keys.upper_bracts: Pleiochasial bracts remain green or are only paler green at the base rather than sharply red/pink/white as is typical of E. cyathophora.
morphology_keys.cyathium: One yellow-green gland, stipitate and clavate, about 1–1.4 × 1–1.2 mm; opening circular, occasionally flattened by pressing, with a distinct annular rim; appendages absent.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 2.8–3.8 × 4–5.3 mm, three-lobed, usually glabrous and only rarely sparsely puberulent.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds broadly deltoid, about 2.4–2.8 × 1.9–2.4 mm, angular in cross section with a strongly keeled dorsal face and tubercles.
best_field_traits: Annual upright herb; can resemble toothed spurges and wild poinsettia.
Upper bracts usually green or paler near base in FNA; colored-looking specimens need recheck.
Leaves extremely variable, from unlobed to deeply cut, often on one specimen.
Terminal green cyathial cups and glabrous three-lobed capsules.
Single clavate stalked nectar gland with round opening and annular rim is main distinction; macro missing.
Texas occurrence comparison-only per existing project, not automatically approved native.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. cyathophora, use the cyathial gland before leaf shape. E. heterophylla = green/pale bracts + stipitate gland + round annular-rimmed opening; E. cyathophora = sharply colored bract bases + sessile/substipitate gland + oblong rimless opening.
morphology_keys.reproductive_teaching: Cyathium = a cup-shaped Euphorbia inflorescence with highly reduced staminate flowers and one pistillate flower. The stalked swelling outside the cup becomes a THREE-LOBED capsule; upper colored or green modified leaves are BRACTS and not five separate petals. Do not mistake a ripe fruit for the nectar gland.
morphology_keys.seed_pair: E. cyathophora seeds are usually rounded in cross section and lack caruncle; E. heterophylla seed is angular, with a strong dorsal keel and small caruncle, as in FNA. These seed structures are absent in existing photographs, so don't put arrows on them.
field_camera_steps: 1. Full plant and full upper shoot with mature leaves.
2. Bract pair top view: colored or green basal patch and leaf attachments, at same scale.
3. Green capsule at branch tip — shoot front and side, include mm scale.
4. MACRO of one cyathium gland with 10–20× or better microscope. Capture aperture opening and whether there is a raised circular rim.
5. For no-bract-color plants, photograph mature seed faces/cross-section and keep group-level ID if gland still missing.
6. Do not tear stem to demonstrate irritating Euphorbia latex to students.
morphology_keys.habitat_management: Annual weed-prone spurge of open/disturbed habitats. Habitat alone doesn't settle nativity. Respect existing project county and introduction labels; milky latex may irritate skin/eyes. Avoid using bract color alone to decide ecological management.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia heterophylla: green or only paler green at base
lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia cyathophora: usually sharply white, pink, or red at base

comparisons.key_distinctions: Heterophylla typically green/pale green bracts + stalked yellow-green gland with ROUND hole and ANNULAR RIM versus cyathophora strongly red/pink/white basal bract (often) + OBLONG rimless aperture. Both vary in bract coloration and leaf outline; check a real enlarged gland. Seed in heterophylla angular with strongly keeled dorsal face and tiny caruncle, compared with cyathophora generally rounded in cross-section and caruncle absent.
crew_key: Is it a Euphorbia: tiny cyathia and separate three-lobed capsules rather than showy normal petals?
Find upper modified bracts; note red/pink/white BASES versus green/pale-green bases, but never conclude on color alone.
Check whether there is one nectar gland on the cyathial cup and photograph its FACE under magnification.
Oblong gland opening, rim absent = cyathophora. Circular opening, annular rim present = heterophylla.
If tiny gland is unresolved, retain E. cyathophora–heterophylla group until clearer proof.

field_comparison_matrix.cyathophora: Often sharply red/pink/white at the base; sometimes fully green
field_comparison_matrix.heterophylla: Usually wholly green or merely pale green at base
Angular section, keeled back, minute caruncle

photo_note: FOUR stored exact-label photos including one TAXON-ID-HOLD Psumuseum candidate; THREE eligible visually checked teaching photographs carry SEVEN real anatomy arrows. Key SAplants actual E. heterophylla var. heterophylla image (CC BY-SA) shows ROUND gland apertures WITH raised annular rims and separate three-lobed fruits. Matching real E. cyathophora SAplants gland photo shows OBLONG rimless openings. The questionable salmon-pink-bracted Psumuseum image is held and MUST NOT be included in public or featured card. Mature seeds with a tiny caruncle, acute dorsal keel, and angular cross section remain a desirable optional macro photo; a local Hays specimen is not required to close field-training work.

items.label: Confirm the circular gland opening and raised rim — real macro
items.image_role: Macro of cyathial gland openings with raised circular rims, green three-lobed developing fruits, original source labelled E. heterophylla var. heterophylla

items.caption: Two conspicuous round yellow-green openings with ring-shaped raised margins are actual cyathial glands; large three-lobed green bodies are separate developing capsules. The glands provide the distinguishing ROUND/RIMMED character of E. heterophylla. The specimens are photographed from a naturalized garden in South Africa, not a Central Texas collection.
items.why_it_matters: Unlike the prior small photos, this one actually demonstrates a real raised circular gland rim so crew can compare the correct botanical part against the oblong rimless gland of E. cyathophora.

items.label: Compare wild poinsettia's OBLONG rimless gland

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Painted spurge: GREEN bracts support, the round gland confirms
steps: Observe usually GREEN or paler-green upper bracts, but don't force an ID from leaf color.
Look at the new high-resolution heterophylla photo: its one yellow-green gland has a CIRCULAR mouth with a raised annular rim.
Compare to the cyathophora photo: its yellow-green gland is a FLATTENED OBLONG trough without a raised circular rim.
Three-lobed green fruits are capsules on BOTH species; they are not gland openings.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Round cyathial gland opening with raised annular rim supports E. heterophylla; oblong rimless gland supports E. cyathophora. The photo pair now actually illustrates BOTH forms.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The old Psumuseum photo at index 1 is ON TAXON-ID HOLD and excluded from featured photo panels and public training regardless of its original Commons label. Real annular gland macro is at image index 3 and is sufficient for field teaching. True mature keeled seed and caruncle remain optional photo gaps.
